data.name: Arishaah
data.gender_notes: Arishaah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Arishaah is a name derived from the Arabic root sh-r-kh which means 'to irrigate' or 'to cultivate'. This name is a reminder of the importance of following the teachings of the Quran and striving to live a righteous and pious life. The one who bears this name is a guardian and cultivator of sacred knowledge, tending to the garden of Islam and nurturing the growth of faith and good deeds.
data.spiritual_meaning: A servant of Allah, devoted to following His guidance
data.etymology: Arishaah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gardener of the sacred law.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Arishaah total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

Historically, it has been used across various Muslim cultures, embodying the values of dignity and respect.

It has been associated with agriculture and the cultivation of crops, reflecting the value of hard work and dedication to the land in many Islamic cultures. This name would have been given to a child who was expected to contribute to the family farm, instilling a sense of responsibility and a work ethic from an early age.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, Arishaah is a reminder of the Islamic concept of the garden of paradise, Al-Jannah. Just as a gardener tends to their crops and nurtures them to reach their full potential, Muslims are called to cultivate their faith, wisdom, and good character to cultivate a paradise in their own lives and contribute to the greater garden of the Islamic community. The name Arishaah also symbolizes the idea of irrigation, reminding us to seek the guidance and sustenance from Allah, the "rainmaker" and "irrigator," who is the source of all life and wisdom.
